thread:
deploy-bot: Release attempt blocked for redwood-inference-server:v2.14.0. SBOM provenance check failed for eu-canary. Failing component: libfasttext@3.2.0 (missing cosign signature). SBOM score=0.78 (threshold=0.9). Action: hold. See /deploy logs: https://ci.internal/1234/build/5678

maya: pinging eng-releases — change window ends in ~2h for the full rollout. need quick triage on whether we pin, hotfix, or carve out EU.

tom: looking. is this a missing signature or a license mismatch?

deploy-bot: scan details -> missing cosign signature on transitive artifact. SBOM metadata lists source=https://third.party/libs/libfasttext-3.2.0.tar.gz but no signature block. No license red flags, just provenance gap.

raj: libfasttext is pulled in by model-serving. there is a 3.2.1 release that was signed last month. we could pin to 3.2.1 in the image.

lina: can we scope the canary to non-EU regions while we fix the EU gate? EU compliance requires signatures for customers in that region.

ben: change window for global release closes in ~4h. carving out EU needs legal + security OK. @sarah can you advise fast?

sarah: missing signature is a blocker for EU-regulated customers. legal may allow a documented exception but that takes time. a preferred path is to produce a signed artifact and re-run SBOM.

tom: ETA to rebuild with libfasttext@3.2.1 and republish image: ~45m. If we do a hotfix image tag (v2.14.0-hotfix1) we will get a new SBOM and rescanned artifact.

maya: alternative quick path: pin the dependency in the Dockerfile and push hotfix tag. will the CI produce a new SBOM automatically?

deploy-bot: yes — CI triggers SBOM generation and cosign verification on push. command used: `./ci/scripts/generate_sbom.sh && cosign verify-blob --keyring=... sbom.json`

tom: starting rebuild + pin now. pushing to `registry.redwood/release/redwood-inference-server:v2.14.0-hotfix1`. logs: https://ci.internal/1234/build/5679

raj: i'll open a small PR to pin the version in the Dockerfile and link to the build. will add a short changelog note.

lina: if rebuild succeeds, can we avoid delaying global rollout? we should still gate EU until signature verified.

sarah: i'll start drafting an emergency exception doc in case rebuild fails, but priority is signed artifact. legal pinged.

ben: decision: try rebuild/hotfix now. if green, re-scan and proceed with global canary but keep EU blocked until SBOM score >= 0.9 and signature verified. if rebuild fails, we do EU carveout + legal exception or delay full release. update release notes to mention the hotfix and SBOM verification outcome.

tom: rebuild finished, pushing image and triggering SBOM scan. CI status: `BUILD SUCCESS -> pushed registry.redwood/...:v2.14.0-hotfix1`

deploy-bot: Re-scan complete for redwood-inference-server:v2.14.0-hotfix1. SBOM score=0.95; cosign signature present for libfasttext@3.2.1. Hold released for canary (non-EU). EU region still gated until final legal attestation.

ben: rolling forward non-EU canary now. EU carveout scheduled — security/legal to confirm by EOD. release notes updated with: "hotfix: pinned libfasttext->3.2.1 and verified SBOM provenance; EU rollout delayed pending attestation."

maya: thanks all. leaving thread open until legal confirms EU status.

sarah: legal gave preliminary ok for documented attestation; will post final note in this thread once signed.

ben: closing action items: (1) raj PR merged to pin dockerfile, (2) tom created hotfix image and CI scanned, (3) maya updated release notes, (4) sarah to paste signed attestation. moving to follow-up if EU sign-off arrives.

deploy-bot: NOTE: if any downstream customers require immediate EU access, open support ticket referencing this thread and link attestation once available.
